problems.problem: Two clarity faults. First, the opening participle dangles: ‘Opening a chapter of conspiracies in Israel, Judah’s Azariah does right’ makes Azariah the one opening the chapter. Second, Rashi’s reading is left without its point. The JPS ‘house set apart’ hides the Hebrew ‘house of freedom’ (בית החפשית), and both commentators play on that word. Metzudat David’s ‘release’ carries the link, but Rashi’s ‘a house he made himself among the graves’ does not. Rashi’s own ground is that the dead are called free (עָשָׂה לוֹ בַּיִת בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אֲמַר בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי), and without it the reader cannot see why graves answer ‘set apart’.
problems.fix: For example: ‘At the head of a chapter of conspiracies in Israel, Judah’s Azariah does right yet is stricken; Metzudat David, on 15:5, reads the ‘house set apart’ as release from the toil of governing, kingship counting, as the sages say, as servitude, and Rashi, on 15:5, as a house among the graves, the dead being called free.’ That is 56 words and passes entry-check (scratch/c3/123-fix.json). Leave src unchanged.

problems.problem: The key verse is printed as ‘In all their affliction He was afflicted’ (the qere, with vav), but Rashi comments on the written text, the ketiv ‘לא צר’ with aleph: לא היצר להם כפי מעלליהם, He did not afflict them as their deeds deserved. As it stands, the sentence says Rashi reads the verse as ‘His not afflicting them’ directly under a translation that says the opposite, and it never says why. Ibn Ezra’s reading (האמת שהוא בוי"ו … כאלו גם הוא היה בצרה) rests on the other spelling. The difference between the two readings is therefore left unexplained, and a reader will take the Rashi clause for a contradiction of the text.
problems.fix: Say that Rashi reads the written ‘not’. For example: ‘Recounting the LORD’s mercies to the house of Israel, the prophet recalls His care for them; Rashi, on 63:9, reading the written ‘not’, takes it as His not afflicting them as their deeds deserved, since Michael, prince of the Presence, always saved them, and Ibn Ezra, on 63:9, as His being distressed, as it were, and so hastening to save.’ That is 60 words, at the two-commentator cap, and passes entry-check (scratch/c3/142-fix.json). Leave src unchanged.
